page: OVHcloud a10-90 is a GPU-accelerated server featuring 60 dedicated AMD EPYC 9554 physical cores running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 85.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.42 GB per core. Graphics processing is handled by two NVIDIA A10 GPUs from the Ampere family, delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and the network interface provides a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 10%. The server also demonstrates top-tier capabilities in LLM inference, achieving top 10% speeds for prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large models. Single-core performance, measured by Geekbench and stress-ng, remains strong in the top 25%. However, memory bandwidth exhibits a clear tradeoff: while small-block cached read-only bandwidth is in the top 10%, large-block uncached read-only bandwidth falls into the middle 50% average.

Given the high density of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and dual NVIDIA A10 GPUs, the server offers high resource density for parallelized compute and graphics workloads. The relatively low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.42 GB per core represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive databases, but the hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for GPU-accelerated tasks. This server is best suited for LLM inference, machine learning workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, and ray tracing applications.
description: The OVHcloud a10-90 is a GPU-accelerated server designed for compute-heavy and graphics-intensive workloads. It features 60 dedicated AMD EPYC 9554 cores operating at 3.3 GHz, paired with 85.0 GB of system memory and a 400 GB local SSD. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA A10 Ampere GPUs providing a total of 48 GB VRAM. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance and exceptional LLM inference speeds across various model sizes. While cached memory bandwidth and multi-threaded decompression rank in the top 10%, the server presents a tradeoff with a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.42 GB and average uncached large-block memory read speeds. This configuration is highly efficient for parallel processing, software compilation, ray tracing, and machine learning inference.
